speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: The Electromyography and Nerve Conduction Study (EMG/NCS) reveals active and chronic denervation changes consistent with anterior horn cell pathology. Specifically, the study shows fibrillation potentials and positive sharp waves in the cervical paraspinal muscles, bilateral C5-T1 myotomes (hands, forearms, and upper arms), with relative sparing of the lower extremities. Nerve conduction studies demonstrate preserved sensory nerve action potentials (SNAPs) and compound muscle action potentials (CMAPs) in the distal nerves, but reduced CMAP amplitudes in the upper extremities, correlating with the observed weakness. These findings support a diagnosis of a cervical cord lesion affecting the motor neurons, consistent with the syrinx identified on your MRI, rather than a peripheral neuropathy or radiculopathy.

speaker: Doctor
text: The EMG/NCS findings confirm anterior horn cell pathology with a syrinx, which aligns perfectly with your symptoms of burning pain, weakness, and preserved sensation. Given the MRI confirmation of a cervical syrinx, likely secondary to your prior motor vehicle accident, I can now provide a definitive conclusion. DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical Syringomyelia
